angle: WR/TE break mechanics from Combine route drills (Break G: how hard a receiver pushes off the ground at the sharpest point of his cut), graded with the same code on NFL snaps of the same route families, tested against full-season separation over expected (SOE) on held-out classes. The positive use is last season's route-shrunk SOE as a day-3 tiebreaker; the tracking is a film description, not a grade.
metric_name: Break G: mean acceleration (g) over the 1.0 s centred on the sharpest point of the first route break, z-scored within drill and Combine year and averaged over route drills; 1 sd = 0.021 g.
headline_number: -1.2 in of season SOE per sd of Break G [90%: -3.6, +1.0], n=116 on unseen classes, so gains above +1 inch are ruled out (TOST at +/-3 in: upper arm p 0.001, lower arm p 0.10). Same-route true correlation 0.02 [-0.27, 0.32], n=99, against a raw 0.34 for the official 40 vs NFL top speed. Day-3 tiebreaker: season-fold gain 0.31 [-0.08, 0.63] over 20 pairs (0.31 with the shrinkage refitted inside each fold; 0.15 [-0.10, 0.40] in draft-class folds); the rule beats naive raw last-season SOE by only 0.09 [-0.19, 0.40]. Matched contrasts 62% [41, 80] of 53, shuffle p 0.14.

open_risks: The day-3 edge is still not proven: the season-fold interval includes 0, draft-class folds halve the gain (0.15), and the rule barely beats naive last-season SOE (0.09 [-0.19, 0.40]).
The frozen_rule_2026.json hash was not committed to git in this run (no commit was requested), and the freeze date (24 October 2026) is after the 2026 season began; the 2026 test has power 0.37.
The bounded null on the drill-to-NFL link is wide: 72% posterior mass within +/-0.2, and TOST at +/-3 in fails on the downside (p 0.10).
Scout notes rest on up to 40 sampled snaps (Douglas has 9); man-minus-zone split reliability is about 0, so the splits are only film prompts.
Not a blind test: all three classes were seen during development; the act-on cut (top four with 14+ games) is a judgement call.
